ephemeris_agreement.scope: 24 sites, Sun and Earth, every 6 h over the site files' data range (2026-01-01 to 2031-01-01)
ephemeris_agreement.reference: Skyfield + JPL DE421 + MOON_ME_DE421 frame (moon_080317.tf, moon_pa_de421_1900-2050.bpc)
ephemeris_agreement.limitation: Compares two computations (JPL Horizons DE441 vs Skyfield DE421), not observations. The differences are mostly the 0.001 deg rounding of the stored angles. Verdict changes count sampled visible/blocked verdicts that flip when the reference positions are run through our horizon.

horizon_method.kind: Method agreement (independent geometry, same elevation data)
horizon_method.scope: 12 of 24 sites (those the south-polar map plane covers), 720 directions each
horizon_method.reference: Straight lines in the polar map plane + central-angle formula (the engine's original method)
horizon_method.limitation: Tests the geometry only: both methods read the same LOLA elevation data, so errors in the terrain data itself are not tested. The differences grow away from the pole, where the flat-map method's straight-line approximation is weakest.

illumination_observed.scope: 4 of 24 sites inside the LROC map (88-90 S); model re-run for the map's period with the sensor at the surface
illumination_observed.limitation: Yearly totals from 2010-11, not the mission dates; a 100 m camera pixel vs a point model. On sharp light/dark edges single points can differ by tens of percentage points; these are observed discrepancies, not a confidence interval.
